The Frontier

From desert outpost to a meadow of machines

Start with a training saber in a dusty trading post. By the end you’ll have crossed a lake by hoverbike, raided an underground lab, teleported to orbit, conquered an ice colosseum and stepped onto a meadow where machines fly. Then the Sage hands you a key, and the real adventure begins: a sea of living lightning, a spire in the clouds, a jade temple and a palace of fire.

These are just some of the places you’ll explore. There’s plenty more of the Frontier to discover for yourself.

Outpost Kessa

Lv 1–10

A wind-scoured trading post on the edge of the Dunes, with a crashed shuttle under its canopy. Your first saber, your first hack, your first Scrap Bot.

Dunewell Mine

Lv 10–49

Twisting tunnels rich in Ferrite and Cobalt, with mine carts, Blissnut trees and hackable Mining Corp mainframes. Rock Mites and Cyborg Scorpions guard the ore, and the dreaded Cyborg King Scorpion waits in the depths.

Neo-Haven

Lv 16–38

A chrome city of glass towers across Lake Vire. Grand hotel, linked bank, and a mayor with secrets.

Orbital Hub Aster

Safe zone

A little town on a giant space hangar in orbit. A glass floor over open space, the Aster Casino, a forge and a whole teleport hub with guides for every destination.

Mirehold

Lv 27–36

A stilt village of gas-masked swamp folk, a candlelit chapel, a taxidermist who mounts everything you defeat and a jade temple rising out of the swamp.

Frostpeak Colosseum

Lv 47–49

An arena carved from glacier ice, packed with cheering spectators. The Eskimo Elder spins in on a snow tornado to summon five waves of Yetis and Cryo Sentinels, then the Glacier Warden itself.

Derelict Lab

Lv 48

A sealed research complex deep under Dunewell Mine. Search the supply lockers for two keycards, drop the laser fence at the far gate and face Zomborg Prime inside his glowing red ring, while Cyborg Zombies shamble through the halls.

Skills

Eight skills. Every one goes to 99.

Progress the classic way: every swing, hack and ore you mine earns experience. Pick a path or master them all, then wear the skillcape to prove it.

  • Start with a pickaxe, turn it into a drill, then upgrade through seven tiers all the way to a Mining Laser.
  • Bury bones from every creature to deepen your Focus, then spend it on attack and defence rituals.
  • Craft full sets of melee and ranged armour at the workbench.
  • Earn a cape with its own emblem for every skill you max.
  • Melee1/99Laser sabers, axes, flails and chainsaws.
  • Ranged1/99Pistols, rifles and bazookas, with real line of sight.
  • Hacking1/99Crack kiosks, mainframes and datavaults for credits.
  • Mining1/99Start with a pickaxe, then build drills for nine ores from Ferrite to Crimsonite, ending with a trio of mining lasers.
  • Gathering1/99Healing Pods, Blissnuts, Glowcaps and festive Bauble Berries.
  • Crafting1/99Smelt bars and forge full armour sets at the workbench.
  • Questing1/99Eighteen quests, from bar brawls to a main story that ends with a party hat.
  • Focus1/99Bury bones, pray at altars, channel combat rituals.
Focus

Bury bones. Bend reality.

Every creature drops bones. Bury them to train Focus, then spend focus points (refilled at any altar) on four kinds of power.

  • ✦
    RitualsCombat buffs you switch on and off. Attack rituals sharpen your accuracy and damage, defence rituals cut how often and how hard you get hit. They drain focus while they run. Fury and Stone from the start, Wrath at Focus 12, Bastion at 18, Ascension at 26 and the Aegis at 32.
  • ✨
    TransmutationFuse two healing items into one stronger one, from humble Healing Pods all the way up to Bauble Berries.
  • ⇶
    Ability powersKinetic Push (Focus 16) blasts nearby enemies into the walls, and Mind Freeze (Focus 26) locks them in place so they can’t move or strike.
  • ☠
    Ability summonsCall a ghostly ally to fight beside you for 15 seconds: a Skeleton at Focus 12, a golden Knight at 24, a Cyborg Samurai at 45 and, for true masters, the Warlock Master at 80 with fire, ice and thunder.
The Armoury

Gear that shows up on your character

Everything you equip is drawn on your hero, from bronze plate to a six-piece insect carapace. Mix melee sets, ranged sets and rare hybrid armour to build your own look.

Crafted weapons

Pick your colour

13 recolourable weapons · 6 colours

Craft a weapon at a workbench and you choose its colour: red, cyan, yellow, orange, purple or white. Its blade or glow, icon, name and every shot it fires all match, and you can keep a whole rack of the same weapon in different colours.

Legendary weapons

Rare drops, secrets, casino jackpots and gold-dyed upgrades. Each one has its own look and effects. 46 weapons in all, from training sabers to plasma pistols that fire glowing goo.

  • ★ Devil Edge
  • ★ Dart of Destruction
  • ★ Twin Reaver Chainsaws
  • ★ Twin Deluxe Chainsaws
  • ★ Gold Reaper Scythe
  • ★ Skyfall Beacon
  • ★ Light Bringer
  • ★ Stormcaller Bolt
  • ★ Cryo Talons
  • ★ Barbed Yo-Yo

Ten armour sets

Five melee sets from Bronze Guard to Abyssal, five ranged sets from Shadow Outlaw to Blaze Vanguard, each crafted from the ore you mine. Bring a full set to the right specialist and they’ll restyle it in one of twenty new finishes: the Wanderer in Dunewell does Bronze Guard, Warlord, Shadow Outlaw and Enforcer (try Steel Plated, Brass, Crimson or Robin Hood), Kira on Orbital Hub Aster handles Abyssal and Blaze Vanguard, and Vanta at the Neo-Haven Armory does the rest, from Dark Paladin to Cyborg Jester and Destroyer.

Boss-only hybrid armour

Hivemind, Shadowveil and Warhunter sets drop only from the Cyborg King Scorpion, the Forgemaster Colossus and the Lava Greatknight, at 1 in 20. They boost melee and ranged at once, once you’re strong enough to wear them.

Skill capes

Max a skill, wear the proof

Reach level 99 in any skill and the Cape Merchant in Dunewell will sell you its skill cape. Every one of the eight capes has its own colours and an emblem on the back: crossed green lightsabers for Melee, a crosshair for Ranged, glowing circuitry for Hacking, a drill for Mining and more.

Capes show on your hero from every angle, flowing behind you as you walk.

And behind the shop hangs the Grandmaster Cape, sealed to its rack by a force nobody understands. Not even the merchant who wove it can move it. Only a hero with every skill at 99 can lift it free.

Player housing

Your own Pocket Dimension

Sign with the estate agent on Orbital Hub Aster and a teleporter folds you into a private Pocket Dimension: a house and garden that are yours to build.

  • A full storefront. The Home Sphere sells 88 pieces of furniture with live previews: beds, gemstone thrones, campfires, fridges, a golden toilet, robot statues, neon signs, a hoverbike stand, casino tables, fences and 19 trophies of the creatures you've defeated.
  • Build mode. Pick a piece, tap a tile, done. It works with a mouse or a thumb, and you can rotate or pick things back up whenever you like.
  • Show off your gear. Armour stands, weapon racks and cape racks display the gear you put on them, and you can take it back any time.
  • Make it yours. Ten garden themes (including a lava-soaked Volcano Land, an Underwater Dome, a Neon Sprawl and a Mountain Top above the clouds), wallpapers, floors, portal styles and waygate skins, plus a working altar, forge, crafting table, waygate and blissnut trees.
The main quest

All eight main quests, in order

The main story takes you from a dusty mining town to a meadow of machines. Play them in this order; each one unlocks the way to the next.

  1. Chapter 1Sting in the Deep

    Starts: Elder Varo — Dunewell Town

    Slay the Cyborg King Scorpion in the depths of Dunewell Mine and earn the right to ride a hoverbike.

  2. Chapter 2Retake the Lab

    Starts: Neon Sprawl

    Hack the laser fence in the Neon Sprawl and take down the six-armed Infiltrator Guardian in Sublevel 9.

  3. Chapter 3Emerald of the Mire

    Starts: Bog Warden — Mirehold

    Help the Bog Warden of Mirehold and claim the Swamp Emerald that opens the hub’s vault.

  4. Chapter 4Bigger They Are…

    Starts: The Foundry

    Fight through the Foundry and topple the Forgemaster Colossus.

  5. Chapter 5Challenger Approaches

    Starts: Eskimo Elder — Frostpeak Summit

    Place the Swamp Emerald and Molten Core on the hub’s pedestals to open the Frostpeak Gate, earn the Eskimo Elder’s blessing, then survive five waves of the Frostpeak Colosseum and fell the Glacier Warden.

  6. Chapter 6I’ve Got the Key...

    Starts: The Sage — Verdant Expanse

    Open the Rusted Bulkhead in Dunewell Mine, defeat Zomborg Prime in the Derelict Lab and teleport to the Verdant Expanse. The Sage hands you the Arc Key: ride the skimmer mech across the living lightning of the Arc Sea and destroy the two Robo Gargoyles atop the Null Spire.

  7. Chapter 7More Gems

    Starts: Hooded hologram — Null Spire Summit

    Take the Swamp Jade from the Werebear’s lair in the Jade Temple and the Lava Ruby from the Lava Palace beyond the Molten Passage, then set both on the Null Spire pedestals to wake the portal.

  8. Chapter 8We Came, We Saw

    Starts: The Null Spire portal

    Step through the portal into Cyberspace and find the Sage waiting on the other side.

Between the battles

Plenty to do off the main path

Pocket Dimension

Buy your own house and garden from the estate agent on Orbital Hub Aster, then fill it from 88 pieces of furniture, trophies, gear racks and jukeboxes that play any song you've heard.

Aster Casino

Play 21 against Dealer Vex or bet on roulette. Hit a single number and win a legendary.

Mortimer’s bestiary

Every creature you defeat gets mounted in the Mirehold taxidermy. Fill twelve pedestals for a Plasma Pistol, and all of them for a vial of Gold Dye.

Bar brawls & heists

Fist-fight Brakk the Brute, find a stolen hotel keycard and expose a corrupt mayor.

Gold Dye

Gild a Buster Axe into the Gold Reaper Scythe, Twin Reaver Chainsaws into Twin Deluxe Chainsaws, or a Skyfall Beacon into the Light Bringer, which calls down pillars of light. Find dye in a locked strongbox, earn it from Mortimer, or pay Vanta a fortune.

Hidden caches

Secrets are tucked into every corner, from a well in Dunewell Mine to a sealed cache in Grimfen Swamp that hides the Toxic Claws.

Traders

Sell crafted gear, and any weapon a merchant stocks, to the Wanderer, the Neo-Haven armory or the hub’s weapons counter when your pack gets full.

Achievements

46 milestones to chase, from First Blood and Boss Rush to Millionaire and Treasure Hunter, each with its own trophy toast.

Your own ship

Hangar Master Juno sells three ships in the Telehub hangar. Paint the hull and trim, change the engine glow, add stripes, flames or a checkerboard, then fly it to the Moon: an optional area only your own ship can reach.

Cracker party hats

Finish the story and pull a cracker with the Sage for a paper party hat in red, blue, green or yellow. Swap colours any time.

Linked banks

Store gear in Dunewell, Neo-Haven, the hub or Mirehold and collect it from any of them.

A chapel quiz

Answer Mother Silt’s four questions to earn the Focus Band and its night-vision goggles.

Original soundtrack

Seventeen original 8-bit themes, from a jungle-drum main menu and a jazz-fusion lab groove to an icy arena battle and a mystic summit hymn, plus sound effects for every weapon. All generated in the browser.

Play anywhere

Built for the desk and the bus

EverSaber runs in any modern browser. Open the link, pick a name and you’re playing in seconds.

On PC

  • Click to walk, fight and interact
  • Side panel for skills, gear and quests
  • World map and illustrated atlas

On phone

  • Full-screen view, portrait or landscape
  • Quick buttons for healing and focus
  • Tap to act, long-press to inspect

Your progress saves in your browser. Export a save file to carry it between devices.
